title:
Planar-Chiral Metal
Clusters Direct Polarization-Responsive
Supercrystals
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Chiral metal clusters are promising atomically precise building blocks for hierarchical chiral materials, but their programmed assembly into structurally resolved supercrystals with traceable chirality transfer remains challenging. Here, we show that planar-chiral Cu5 clusters can serve as symmetry-defined modules for constructing polarization-responsive supercrystals. Through single-site capping control and symmetry-matched linker-directed coordination assembly, the Cu5 unit is organized into monomeric, dimeric, trimeric, and helical crystalline architectures, thereby enabling chirality to be traced from discrete clusters to higher-order supercrystalline structures. Single-crystal analyses reveal how the planar chirality of the cluster is encoded locally and propagated through distinct, orientationally ordered packing sequences. Quantitative Mueller matrix measurements show architecture-dependent circular and linear optical responses, including circular and linear retardance, which correlate with the crystallographic orientation and packing sequence of the Cu5 units, particularly Cu···Cu bonding. This work establishes planar-chiral metal clusters as versatile, stereochemically programmable synthons, providing a quantitative framework that links cluster-level chirality, arrangement orientation, and macroscopic polarization-dependent optical responses. The strategy offers a novel modular route to structurally defined chiral supercrystals, in which optical polarization responses can be traced to atomically resolved anisotropic sequences of chiral cluster assembly.</jats:p>
journal:
Journal of the American
Chemical Society

title:
Correlative Multidimensional
Tracking and Modeling
Reveals Mechanical Regulation of Nanoparticle Endocytosis
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Understanding nanoparticle–membrane interactions during endocytosis is critical for advancing nanomedicine. However, a comprehensive understanding of its dynamic complexity remains elusive, largely due to limitations in often oversimplified theoretical models and experimental challenges in correlating nanoparticle conformations and protein assemblies. To bridge this persistent theoretical–experimental divide, we developed an integrated approach combining multidimensional single-particle tracking with theoretical modeling for understanding clathrin-mediated endocytosis of rod-shaped nanoparticle cargos in live cells. Real-time tracking reveals a characteristic seesaw-like rotational motion of nanocargos that is temporally correlated with clathrin and dynamin recruitment, enabling the endocytic process to be classified into six distinct stages. Theoretical modeling, informed by these experimental observations, identifies orientation-dependent energy preferences arising from the interplay between membrane-associated effects and clathrin lattice elasticity, yielding orientation trends consistent with experimental observations. By focusing on this core structural framework, our work establishes a quantitative foundation for understanding how geometric and mechanical interactions govern the nanoparticle internalization. This correlative experimental and theoretical work is exemplary of the renewed efforts to establish closer connections between experimental evidence and theoretical modeling with higher biological complexity.</jats:p>
journal:
Journal of the American
Chemical Society

title:
Structural and Electronic
Properties of Lead Halide
Perovskite Thin-Film Surfaces
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Polycrystalline perovskite thin films are consistently associated with high-performance optoelectronic devices. The main challenges currently under the spotlight lie with the stability and reliability of these devices, requiring a better understanding of thin-film surfaces and interfaces. However, their consistent investigation is often very challenging. Given the soft nature of these materials, there is a struggle to directly assign the origin of the electronic features and correlate them to the chemical nature of the surfaces. Here, by exploiting a multimodal approach, we measure for the first time, at submicrometer scales, the diffraction patterns of the thin-film grain surface, which provide the material fingerprint and experimental evidence that the surface of such soft semiconductors is not as disordered as often claimed. Then, building on such knowledge, we move to ultraviolet photoemission spectroscopy, which provides information about the electronic structure of the first few nanometers of the thin-film surface. Having identified the structural nature of the surface, we are eventually able to unambiguously assign the origin of the photoemission spectra for a wide range of metal halide perovskites. In particular, metallic lead is identified to be the origin of the often-reported midgap photoemissive states, thus far assigned to deep electronic states within the halide perovskite semiconductor band gap. The chemical composition of the metal halides, the photodegradation of the perovskites under visible light, the quality of the precursors, and the actual stoichiometry of the thin film heavily define the presence of such states and elucidate the origin of carrier loss, photodegradation, and sample reproducibility in metal halide perovskite optoelectronics.</jats:p>
journal:
Journal of the American
Chemical Society

title:
Detecting Catalytically
Competent Surface-Bound Hydrogen
on Electrocatalysts with Weak Acids
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>The characterization of catalytically competent molecular metal-hydride intermediates distinguishes mechanistic possibilities in reductive molecular electrocatalysis. While surface-bound hydrogen is invoked in several heterogeneous electrocatalytic schemes, the synthetic and spectroscopic tools to establish catalytic competence in molecular systems are not readily translated to surfaces. Molecular systems offer uniform and well-defined active sites; however, surface systems consist of multiple possible binding sites. Here, we discover that the judicious choice of the proton donor enables the independent generation and characterization of catalytically competent surface-bound hydrogen using hydrogen evolution as a model reaction. Using dimethyl sulfoxide, a solvent where Brønsted acid pKa values are well-characterized, and Ag electrocatalysts, compatible with surface-enhanced infrared absorption spectroscopy (SEIRAS), we find that acids with pKa values higher than the protonated solvent generate spectroscopic signatures consistent with the reductive formation of long-lived and linearly bound hydrogen. Conversely, stronger acids that protonate the solvent do not give rise to detectable surface-bound hydrogen, and instead, yield electrokinetic data consistent with hydrogen evolution proceeding via rate-limiting formation of the same linearly bound surface hydrogen. By independently generating the Ag-bound hydrogen with a weak, general acid and subsequently introducing a stronger acid that protonates the solvent, we show that the accumulated surface-bound hydrogen is catalytically competent for hydrogen production via specific-acid-coupled electron transfer. Our work demonstrates that catalytically competent surface-bound hydrogen intermediates in heterogeneous electrocatalysis can be detected and characterized through the strategic choice of the proton donor.</jats:p>
journal:
Journal of the American
Chemical Society

title: A Mirror-Image L-RNA Aptamer Targeting Hypoxia-Inducible Factor-1α Promoter G-Quadruplex Potentiates Tumor Radiotherapy In Vivo
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>The hypoxia-inducible factor (HIF) coordinates the response of tumors to low oxygen by stimulating genes involved in metabolism and angiogenesis. HIF pathway activation is highly associated with tumor progression and radiotherapy resistance. Ligands that target this pathway are potential agents for the treatment of solid tumor malignancies. We developed an L-RNA aptamer, L-Apt5–4, targeting the HIF-1α promoter DNA G-quadruplex (dG4) via mirror-image SELEX. This L-RNA aptamer adopts a stem-loop secondary structure, binds HIF-1α dG4 with high affinity and specificity, and enters the nucleus to effectively downregulate HIF-1α and its downstream targets in cancer cells. By suppressing HIF-1α, L-Apt5–4 not only inhibits tumor cell proliferation, migration, and invasion, but also acts as a potent radiosensitizer, synergizing with radiotherapy to enhance cancer cell death. The combination therapy significantly suppresses tumor growth and metastasis while exhibiting excellent biosafety in vivo. Thus, L-Apt5–4 represents a novel HIF-1α-targeted therapeutic and radiosensitizer for combined cancer treatment.</jats:p>
journal:
Journal of the American
Chemical Society

title: Thiol-ene Radical Polymerizations of Regio - and Stereo -Isomers of a CO2-Derived δ-Lactone Leading to High Molar Mass Polythioethers
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Thiol-ene radical polymerization of CO2-derived lactones containing α,δ-dienes offers a route to sustainable polythioethers with up to 20 wt % CO2. The direct product from CO2/1,3-butadiene telomerization is 3-ethylidene-6-vinyltetrahydro-2H-pyran-2-one ((E)EVP) whose α-alkylidene group causes poor reaction kinetics and nonquantitative alkene conversion with dithiols affording low molar mass polythioethers. Here, we use 3,6-divinyltetrahydro-2H-pyran-2-one (DVP) which was synthesized from the base-catalyzed contrathermodynamic α,β- to β,γ-photodeconjugation of EVP, resulting in the transformation of the α-alkylidene to an α-vinyl functional group. This subtle regio-isomerization was found to result in a 17-fold and 8-fold increase in the rate of α- and δ-ene consumption, respectively, owing to the relative stability of the intermediate carbon-centered radicals. Leveraging these rapid kinetics, high molar mass polythioethers (34 kDa) could be prepared via thiol-ene step-growth polymerization of DVP with 2,2’-(ethylenedioxy)diethanethiol. These molar masses are 10-fold higher than the upper limits obtained with the EVP-derived counterpart, and the polythioethers display mechanical performance suitable as a pressure sensitive adhesive.</jats:p>
journal:
Journal of the American
Chemical Society

title:
Electronic Polarization
of Covalent Organic Framework
Membranes for Precise Antibiotic Purification
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Precise molecular separation is essential for pharmaceutical production and purification, yet existing sieving systems struggle to distinguish structurally similar molecules due to their predominant reliance on size exclusion. Herein, we fabricate a covalent organic framework (COF) membrane featuring fluorine-induced polarized nanochannels for fast organic solvent nanofiltration. The incorporation of fluorine atoms redistributes electron density along the pore walls, creating a polarized electrostatic environment while lowering surface energy. This unique pore environment promotes the uptake and transport of polar solvents, while enhancing separation selectivity by retarding highly polar solutes through polarity-dependent solute-framework interactions. Furthermore, the low surface energy imparted by the robust C–F bonds also reduces irreversible foulant adhesion and facilitates permeance recovery after cleaning. The resultant COF membrane achieves a molecular weight cutoff down to 350 Da and stable operation for over 550 h. Notably, it differentiates structurally related fluoroquinolone antibiotics according to their molecular polarity and delivers a favorable separation factor of 8.9 for norfloxacin over its synthetic intermediate piperazine. This work demonstrates that engineering pore-wall polarity in COF membranes provides a viable route to chemically regulated molecular recognition beyond size-based separation.</jats:p>
journal:
Journal of the American
Chemical Society

title:
Antiaromaticity for
Through-Space Molecular Thermoelectricity
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Charge transport in molecular junctions has largely relied on aromatic frameworks, where intramolecular π-delocalization stabilizes the electronic structure but inherently limits intermolecular electronic coupling. Here we show that antiaromatic Ni(II) norcorrole assemblies outperform their aromatic counterparts in thermally driven charge transport. This superior performance arises from strong intermolecular coupling, facilitated by the externalized electronic stabilization of antiaromatic building blocks. Such strong intermolecular coupling enables unusually thick molecular stacks within molecular junctions and yields Seebeck coefficients of up to 600 μV K–1, far exceeding those of the aromatic analogue. Quantum transport calculations reveal that π–π stacking in the antiaromatic assemblies shifts the HOMO transmission resonance closer to the Fermi level while progressively narrowing it, accounting for the substantial enhancement of the Seebeck coefficient while maintaining efficient long-range charge transport with a low tunneling attenuation coefficient. These findings establish antiaromaticity as a design principle for thermoelectric energy conversion based on collective intermolecular coupling rather than isolated molecular orbitals.</jats:p>
journal:
Journal of the American
Chemical Society

title:
Zeolite Crystallization
via Seed-Mediated Chemical
Vapor Deposition
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>The demand for zeolites with specific, tailored characteristics is expected to further accelerate. For decades, however, zeolites have been predominantly synthesized by hydrothermal methods, in which tightly coupled sol–gel processes, nucleation, and crystal growth constrain property control and complicate device-oriented fabrication. Here we report the direct synthesis of zeolites by chemical vapor deposition (CVD), in which vapor-delivered precursors crystallize on preexisting zeolite seeds. Mechanistic investigations reveal that zeolite growth under CVD follows a fundamentally distinct pathway, where vapor-phase hydrolysis–condensation reactions are spatially decoupled from interfacial crystallization. This decoupling enables the maintenance of a controlled and steady supersaturation, offering a facile strategy for fabricating zeolite films with low dielectric constants and robust mechanical properties. The unique mechanism and operation mode of CVD bring zeolite crystallization into a manufacturing-relevant vapor-phase regime that could be extended to other zeolite types and deployed in diverse applications.</jats:p>
journal:
Journal of the American
Chemical Society

title: Hydration Shell Structure and Water-Mediated Binding of Closo -Dodecaborates Probed by Raman Hydration-Shell Spectroscopy
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>The binding of closo-dodecaborates, B12X122– (where X = H, Cl, Br, I), to solutes and interfaces has widely been attributed to a water-mediated (super)chaotropic effect. The role of water, however, has so far been inferred only indirectly from thermodynamic measurements. Herein, we employ Raman hydration-shell spectroscopy in the OH stretch region to investigate B12X122– in aqueous solution. Specifically, we elucidate (i) the water structure in the hydration shell, (ii) its temperature dependence, and (iii) the water release upon superchaotropic binding. The hydration-shell spectra reveal that all dodecaborates give rise to a sharp Raman band close to 3600 cm–1. This feature is strongly blue-shifted compared to bulk water and represents weakly H-bonded, “almost dangling” OH groups in the hydration shell. Heating is found to blue-shift the hydration water resonance less than the bulk water resonance. Hydration and bulk water resonances thus become more similar at high temperature. This trend reflects a progressively reduced difference in hydrogen-bonding energy upon heating between hydration and bulk water, and is opposite to that of hydrophobic hydration. Furthermore, hydration difference spectra in the presence of the nonionic polymer hydroxypropyl cellulose (HPC) reveal that weakly H-bonded hydration water is released from B12X122– upon superchaotropic binding, together with more strongly H-bonded hydration water from the hydration shells of both B12X122– and HPC. These findings identify weakly bound hydration water, its weak temperature dependence, and its spontaneous release upon binding as molecular hallmarks of the superchaotropic behavior of B12X122–.</jats:p>
journal:
Journal of the American
Chemical Society

title:
Proton-Coupled Electrostatic
Regulation of Anion Electrosorption
in Electric Double Layers
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Electric double layers underpin electrochemical energy storage and modulate interfacial reactivity through the organization of ions and solvent molecules. However, regulating anion accumulation at compact aqueous interfaces while limiting parasitic water reactions remains challenging. Here, anodic polarization reconstructs oxygen-deficient TiO2–x into a depth-graded architecture comprising a rutile interior, a disordered interlayer, and a thin crystalline anatase surface. This architecture establishes an internal electric field that promotes subsurface proton accumulation, creating a responsive charge distribution that regulates anion electrosorption and moderates lateral anion interactions. The thin crystalline surface complements this electrostatic regulation by extending the accessible anodic operating range, combining enhanced interfacial charge storage with high-voltage aqueous operation. Symmetric aqueous supercapacitors sustain cycling over 3.0 V in neutral Na2SO4 for 45,000 cycles and over 2.7 V in natural seawater. These findings identify subsurface ionic chemistry as a design variable for regulating anion electrosorption at aqueous oxide interfaces.</jats:p>
journal:
Journal of the American
Chemical Society

title: Disrupting Hidden Antiaromaticity in N -Hydroxyphthalimide Reveals a Design Principle for Highly Reactive N -Oxyl Hydrogen Atom Transfer Mediators
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>N-hydroxyphthalimide (NHPI) and its corresponding N-oxyl radical, phthalimide N-oxyl (PINO), have long been used as mediators for hydrogen atom transfer (HAT), particularly in radical-mediated C–H oxidations. Although numerous NHPI/PINO derivatives have been developed, the absence of an intuitive model connecting scaffold structure to intrinsic HAT reactivity has left catalyst development largely empirical. Herein, we show that insertion of a heteroatom between one carbonyl group of the NHPI/PINO framework and the fused aryl ring substantially accelerates HAT in electrochemically driven oxidations, with rate enhancements of up to 36-fold for benzylic alcohol substrates. This enhanced reactivity correlates with significantly larger computed O–H bond dissociation enthalpies relative to NHPI (ΔBDEO–H = 6.5–8.1 kcal/mol), which increase the thermodynamic driving force for HAT by the corresponding N-oxyl radicals. NICS, NBO, and DFT-based structural analyses support a model in which previously overlooked antiaromatic destabilization within the five-membered imide motif weakens the O–H bond of NHPI and is relieved upon formation of PINO. Among the heteroatom-containing analogues examined, sulfur-containing N-hydroxythiobenzouracil (NHTBU) provided a favorable balance of high HAT reactivity and catalyst persistence, enabling the electrochemical oxidation of numerous substrates under mild conditions with activity superior to NHPI.</jats:p>
journal:
Journal of the American
Chemical Society

title:
Regulating Functionalized
MXene Crystal-Field Splitting
toward Efficient Bifunctional Oxygen Electrocatalysis of Lithium–Oxygen
Batteries
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>MXenes offer fast conductive frameworks with abundant intrinsic active metal sites, making them promising cathode catalysts for lithium–oxygen batteries for addressing sluggish oxygen kinetics and severe cathode passivation. However, the predictive electronic descriptors for rationally regulating these intrinsic active sites remain elusive. Here, we demonstrate the implementation of crystal-field splitting engineering at Ti sites of Ti3C2-MXene to achieve bifunctional oxygen electrocatalysis. Through coordinated anionic and cationic modifications, we regulate the local coordination environment of Ti atoms, weakening crystal-field splitting and promoting electron delocalization within Ti3C2-MXene frameworks. X-ray absorption spectra reveal systematic shifts of Ti K-edge and contraction of the pre-edge splitting, consistent with weakened and distorted Ti ligand fields. This electronic rearrangement promotes an asymmetric Li2O2 adsorption configuration, thereby lowering the energy barriers for both ORR and OER. Consequently, the functionalized Cu–Ti3C2Br2 delivers a high discharge specific capacity of 11,662 mAh g–1 and reduces the initial charge overpotential by 50% compared with Ti3C2OF. This study indicates crystal-field splitting as a key descriptor governing oxygen electrocatalytic behavior in lithium–oxygen batteries.</jats:p>
journal:
Journal of the American
Chemical Society

title:
Expanding Chemical Space Enables Data–Driven
Structure–Activity Relationships in Cage Catalysis
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Data-driven approaches are increasingly popular in catalysis, supplementing and even replacing traditional strategies that relied on empirical optimization. However, their application in the field of bioinspired cage catalysis remains largely unexplored, primarily due to the limited chemical space of known catalytically active cages. As a result, mechanistic insights are often obtained using computationally intensive DFT calculations on a handful of structurally similar cages. As chemical systems grow in complexity, this approach becomes impractical. Herein, we report a framework that significantly expedites the exploration of a much wider structural landscape while offering computational insights. This is made possible by a novel in situ experimental procedure─which circumvents the traditional time-consuming process of prepare, isolate, characterize, and test─coupled with data-driven methods to identify molecular features that govern activity. Using this approach, we experimentally explore 30 unique PdnL2n cages (n = 2–4) that mediate a nitro-aldol reaction with activities spanning over 4 orders of magnitude. Using this data set, a random forest model trained on molecular descriptors was developed to predict ΔG‡ (MAE of 0.4 kcal mol–1 and R2 = 0.9). SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis highlighted geometric preorganization and electrostatic interactions within the cage as key determinants of catalytic efficiency. Moreover, DFT calculations on a selection of cages further validated these insights, indicating that meaningful mechanistic understanding can be achieved at significantly reduced computational cost. We anticipate that this integrated, screening, data-driven, mechanistic strategy will provide a blueprint workflow for understanding metal–organic cage reactivity and encourage the generation of more comprehensive structural data sets, ultimately enabling the rational design of improved catalytic architectures.</jats:p>
journal:
Journal of the American
Chemical Society

title:
Buried
Interfacial Transport Governs Oxide-Protected
Electrocatalysis
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Protective overlayers are widely used to stabilize metal catalysts under harsh electrochemical conditions. Unlike graphene coatings, oxide overlayers introduce a buried metal-oxide interface that fundamentally reshapes reaction pathways by separating proton delivery from product release. Although proton transport through oxides has been extensively investigated, the fate of reaction products at buried interfaces remains unresolved; for example, H2-molecule vs H-atom pathways remain under debate in oxide-protected hydrogen evolution. Here, we revisit this buried interface using a microelectrochemical cell with well-defined model structures. Systematic measurements across nine metal-oxide heterostructures, combined with density functional theory calculations, reveal that product transport is governed by two sequential kinetic barriers: hydrogen spillover across the metal-oxide junction and hydrogen permeation through the oxide lattice. These coupled barriers determine whether reaction products are released, accumulate at buried interfaces, or induce interfacial failure. This work not only identifies superior Pt-TiO2 and Pd-TiO2 but also clarifies which step is impeded in Au-TiO2, Pt-SiO2, Pt-HfO2, Pd-SiO2, Pd-HfO2, Au-SiO2, and Au-HfO2 heterostructures. Guided by these model studies, we implement a TiO2 protection strategy in a proton-exchange-membrane water electrolyzer with remarkable durability. These findings provide a framework for constructing a complete proton-to-product route for buried interfaces, potentially resolving long-standing ambiguities in oxide-protected electrocatalysis.</jats:p>
journal:
Journal of the American
Chemical Society

title:
Bandedge-State-Limited
Single-Photon Emission from
Volumetric Quantum Design of 2D Colloidal Quantum Wells
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Present-day solution-processable single-photon sources are dominated by three-dimensionally confined colloidal quantum emitters, yet their particle-to-particle variation in single-exciton properties limits reproducibility and scalability. Here, to avoid such heterogeneity, we demonstrate reliable room-temperature single-photon emission from atomically flat two-dimensional (2D) colloidal quantum wells (CQWs) with inherently uniform one-dimensional quantum confinement, despite their long-standing limitations of efficient multiexciton emission and pronounced exciton-surface susceptibility. We resolve these challenges through volumetric quantum design (VQD) of CQWs, yielding a highly localized, single bandedge state. This design laterally confines the bandedge excitonic domain within the exciton coherent area and vertically decouples it from surface states via a thick, strain-relieved quantum-barrier shell that preserves strong confinement, overcoming the daunting thickness-confinement trade-off in 2D CQWs. Statistical single-particle spectroscopy reveals that VQD-CQWs deliver near-blinking-free (on-time: &gt;99.5%) and fluence-insensitive antibunching (g(2)(0): ∼0.041), protected by a bandedge-state-filling bottleneck, together with linear polarization of up to 73% under cavity-free conditions, originating from synergistic transition-dipole and electric-field anisotropies. These advances establish 2D CQWs as a viable, homogeneous and scalable platform for quantum technologies.</jats:p>
journal:
Journal of the American
Chemical Society

title:
Click-Functionalizable
Tetrathiafulvalene-Tetrathiolate
Diradicaloids as Modular NIR-II Fluorophores
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Near-infrared (NIR) emissive fluorophores are appealing for biological imaging and sensing applications, particularly in the lower-energy NIR-II region (1000–1700 nm). Compared to light in the visible and NIR-I regions, NIR-II light undergoes less absorption and scattering by biological tissues, enabling deeper tissue penetration and higher imaging resolution. Tetrathiafulvalene-tetrathiolate (TTFtt)-bridged bimetallic diradicaloid complexes exhibit bright NIR-II emission with high photoluminescence quantum yields (PLQYs) relative to other NIR-II fluorophores. These complexes are also particularly modular, as the capping ligands on the metal centers can be substituted to impart desired properties. Here, azide-functionalized bis(imino)acenaphthene (BIAN) capping ligands are introduced to leverage and expand this modularity. BIAN-capped TTFtt complexes exhibit chemical and photophysical properties comparable to previously reported TTFtt complexes. BIAN backbones functionalized with an azide group further enable Huisgen cycloaddition “click” chemistry for the attachment of diverse functional moieties while preserving the intrinsic NIR-II photophysical properties of the TTFtt core. As one example, a sulfonate-clicked TTFtt complex (1-C3) displays enhanced solubility and increased photoluminescence (PL) intensity in aqueous solutions compared to other TTFtt complexes. Notably, 1-C3 also exhibits pH-dependent PL intensity, suggesting its potential utility as an NIR-II-emitting pH sensor. Furthermore, the enhanced water solubility of 1-C3 enabled us to obtain in vivo gastrointestinal imaging in murine models. Overall, these results demonstrate the dramatically expanded modularity of TTFtt complexes through the use of clickable-BIAN ligands.</jats:p>
journal:
Journal of the American
Chemical Society

title: Extraction-Limited Charge Loss in Tin-Based Perovskite Solar Cells
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Tin-based perovskite solar cells (PSCs) present a promising lead-free alternative for photovoltaics, yet their performance remains markedly inferior to that of lead-based counterparts. A limited understanding of the underlying differences in charge transport dynamics between tin- and lead-based PSCs continues to impede efforts to overcome the reduced open-circuit voltage (Voc) and fill factor (FF) characteristic of tin-based devices. Here, using bias-modulated electrical transient measurements, we reveal a previously neglected extraction-limited charge loss mechanism in tin-based PSCs (efficiency &gt; 14%) that is not evident in lead-based counterparts (&gt; 25%) and fundamentally constrains both Voc and FF. Under high forward bias, the defects and their associated self-doping at the perovskite/electron transport layer interface severely reduce charge extraction efficiency by limiting the extraction of low-mobility carriers due to bulk field screening, which in turn leads to reduced collection efficiency as the unextracted carriers are forced into nonradiative recombination. This mechanism explains the low Voc and FF in tin-based PSCs and underscores interfacial doping control as critical for further performance enhancement.</jats:p>
journal: ACS Energy Letters

title: Low-Temperature CO2 Desorption Enables Ammonium Carbonate Electrolysis Beyond pH Swing Limits
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Bipolar membrane (BPM) electrolysis enables direct conversion of carbon capture solutions to fuels, eliminating energy-intensive CO2 purification and compression. However, CO2 desorption from potassium carbonate limits Faradaic efficiency (FE), with a theoretical maximum CO FE of 50% due to stoichiometric constraints. Here, we examine aqueous ammonia as an alternative carbon capture solution, where CO2 desorption can be enhanced using low-grade waste heat. Gas-phase CO2 release from 1 M ammonium carbonate increases 7.7-fold from 20 to 65 °C, increasing CO FE from 32 to 53% at 100 mA cm–2. This enhancement is consistent with increased CO2 availability from temperature-sensitive NH3–CO2–H2O equilibria. Using a hydrophilic SiO2-decorated Ni single-atom catalyst, we achieve 84% CO FE at 100 mA cm–2 with 2 M ammonium carbonate at 50 °C and 3 bar. Integration with a carbon capture absorber enables stable operation and electrolyte recapture, establishing a closed-loop capture-conversion process.</jats:p>
journal: ACS Energy Letters

title: Multifunctional Dendrimer Interlayers for Tin-Based Perovskite Solar Cells: Inducing Interfacial Dipoles and Suppressing Electrode Corrosion
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Tin-based perovskite solar cells (Sn-PSCs) offer eco-friendly optoelectronics but suffer from low efficiency and ambient instability. Here, we introduce a second-generation poly(amidoamine) (PAMAM) dendrimer interlayer between the C60/BCP electron transport layer and the Ag top electrode. Electrostatic field orientation induced by the metallic electrode activates a PAMAM dipole that shifts the effective interface work function by ∼0.55 eV. This modification of the interfacial energetics is accompanied by an increase in the open-circuit voltage (VOC) by ∼50 mV and is consistent with reduced contact-induced energetic losses. Additionally, the dendrimer forms a physical/chemical barrier against iodine-mediated electrode corrosion. Consequently, unencapsulated Sn-PSCs retain 80% of their initial power conversion efficiency (PCE) after 1000 h in ambient air (∼30 °C, 20–35% RH), a benchmark stability also demonstrated here for Sn–Pb PSCs. This electrode-induced dipole orientation presents a generalizable strategy for boosting efficiency and operational durability in lead-free perovskite photovoltaics.</jats:p>
journal: ACS Energy Letters

title: From Nonstep to Step: Voltage‑Response‑Driven Interfacial Evolution and Closed‑Pore Sodium Filling in Hard Carbon Anode
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Hard carbon (HC) is regarded as the most commercially viable anode for sodium-ion batteries. However, during the initial discharge of the HC anode, the thick solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) derived from the decomposition of the ester-based electrolytes severely restricts sodium storage kinetics. Herein, we propose a customized discharge strategy that triggers a step voltage response (SR) in the HC anode to achieve rapid interfacial passivation. Through multiscale characterizations and theoretical calculations, we elucidate the underlying mechanism: the field-induced concentration effect within the interfacial electrolyte steers the decomposition pathways toward inorganic products, favoring the formation of a thin, uniform, and highly ionically conductive SEI. The accelerated interfacial kinetics significantly lowers the diffusion barrier, thereby enhancing the accessibility of closed pores for quasi-metallic sodium cluster storage. Consequently, the SR-treated HC anode delivers improved rate performance in both the sodium-ion full battery and hybrid capacitor. This study offers critical insights into the design of the formation protocol and provides a facile field-modulated strategy to enhance the sodium storage kinetics of the HC anode.</jats:p>
journal: ACS Energy Letters

title:
Role
of Support Facets and Interparticle Contacts
in Pt Single-Atom Dynamics on Anatase TiO2 Catalysts
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Isolated metal sites in single-atom catalysts (SACs) are dynamic under reaction conditions, yet the role of support features in their redistribution remains to be clarified. Here, using in situ CO-probe diffuse reflectance infrared Fourier transform spectroscopy (DRIFTS) and in situ electron microscopy, we reveal that Pt single atoms on anatase TiO2 surfaces redistribute in a facet- and environment-dependent manner. Increasing the H2 reduction temperature from 250 to 450 °C decreases CO-accessible Pt sites, consistent with Pt migration from TiO2(101) surfaces to TiO2(001) facets associated with interparticle TiO2–TiO2 interfaces and diffusion into subsurface regions. This loss tracks exposed TiO2(001) coverage, but in shape-controlled TiO2 particles, oriented attachment at (001) interfaces suppresses effective facet exposure and preserves Pt accessibility. CO oxidation restores accessible Pt single atoms, revealing a single-atom analogue of strong metal–support interaction. These findings identify that facet abundance and accessibility jointly control single-atom mobility, stability, and catalytic state.</jats:p>
journal: ACS Nano

title:
Vertically Emitted
Near-Infrared Perovskite Chiral
Lasing via a Planar Bound State in the Continuum
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Circularly polarized (CP) coherent light sources are indispensable for quantum information, optical communications, and spintronics. Metasurfaces supporting bound states in the continuum (BICs) offer a promising platform, but planar BIC designs have so far been limited to extrinsic chirality. Such chirality simultaneously produces two oblique beams with opposite helicities on either side of the surface normal, leaving vertically emitted intrinsic chiral lasing with high purity unrealized without complex out-of-plane symmetry breaking. Here, we demonstrate a single-layer planar metasurface that overcomes this barrier by simultaneously breaking in-plane C2 and mirror symmetries, precisely positioning a circularly polarized center (C point) at the Γ-point. This yields strong vertical chiral resonance with a near-unity theoretical degree of circular polarization (DCP), without any out-of-plane symmetry breaking. When integrated with achiral perovskites, our strategy enables the first near-infrared chiral lasing from perovskites and, more critically, the first vertically emitted chiral lasing from planar metasurfaces, delivering a luminescence dissymmetry factor (glum) above 1.5 with no external optical components. This resolves the longstanding trade-off between planar integration and polarization purity, providing a robust, CMOS-compatible strategy for on-chip CP light sources in advanced photonic technologies.</jats:p>
journal: ACS Nano

title:
Subcapsular Sinus
Macrophage Transcytosis Enables
Efficient Intralymphnode mRNA Delivery
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Lymph node (LN)-targeted mRNA vaccines hold promise for cancer immunotherapy, but their efficacy is constrained by limited parenchymal delivery imposed by the lymphatic endothelial barrier of the subcapsular sinus (SCS). The SCS is populated by macrophages that efficiently capture pathogens, raising the question of whether this innate surveillance mechanism can be repurposed for vaccine transport─provided internalized nanoparticles can be rerouted from lysosomal degradation toward transcytosis. Here, we show that yeast cell wall–coated lipid nanoparticles (YCW-LNPs) reprogram SCS macrophages to mediate efficient transcytosis, enabling active delivery into the LN parenchyma and achieving approximately 21-fold higher LN accumulation than unmodified LNPs. Co-encapsulating ovalbumin (OVA) mRNA and the STING agonist MSA-2, YCW-LNPs preferentially accumulate in LNs, drive robust mRNA expression (14.5-fold and 7.4-fold higher than free mRNA and unmodified LNPs, respectively), and concurrently activate the STING pathway to amplify antigen-specific immune responses. In intradermal and lung-metastatic B16-OVA melanoma models, YCW-LNPs achieves marked tumor inhibition (up to 99.0%), prolong survival, and induce durable immune memory protecting mice against tumor rechallenge 60 days after treatment. This pathogen-inspired strategy converts SCS macrophages from degradative sinks into active transporters, offering a generalizable platform for delivering mRNA vaccines and immunomodulators to the LN parenchyma.</jats:p>
journal: ACS Nano

title:
Inverted-Mode Scanning
Tunneling Microscopy for Atomically
Precise Fabrication
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Scanning Tunneling Microscopy (STM) enables fabrication of atomically precise structures with growing technological potential. However, reproducible manipulation of covalently bonded atoms requires control over the atomic configuration of both sample and probe–a challenge in STM. Here, we introduce inverted-mode STM, an approach that enables mechanically controlled chemical reactions for atomically precise fabrication. Tailored molecules on a Si(100) surface enable imaging of extended regions of an annealed probe apex, providing direct experimental access to the probe structure relevant to fabrication. The molecules can also react with the probe, with the two sides of the tunnel junction acting as reactants positioned with subangstrom precision. This allows abstraction or donation of atoms from or to the probe. We demonstrate this by using an alkynyl-terminated molecule to reproducibly abstract hydrogen atoms from the probe at zero volts. We then show that successive reactions can replace specific hydrogen atoms with iodine, followed by removal and manipulation of iodine. The approach is expected to extend to other elements, moieties, and materials, enabling sequential, site-selective chemistry for atomically precise fabrication.</jats:p>
journal: ACS Nano

title:
Leveraging Parameter
Coupling for Signal Enhancement
and Early Detection of Battery Thermal Runaway
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Lithium-ion batteries are vital power sources, but the risk of thermal runaway remains a major safety concern. Existing sensor early-warning systems struggle to detect the localized and rapid evolution of internal failures, leading to inadequate time for preemptive intervention. Here, we present a thermal runaway sensor engineered with a temperature–pressure dual-signal coupling mechanism. The proposed strategy can capture the coupled temperature–pressure signals within the battery pack, thereby enabling the detection of the precursors of battery failure. The sensor can detect abnormal signals about 40 min before the thermal runaway. Translating lab research to industry, we integrated the sensor into commercial large-capacity 314 A h cells. Coupled with a custom-built data acquisition system, the system underwent rigorous validation over 12 months in an energy storage facility under actual conditions. The dual-signal sensing strategy offers an approach for early warning of battery thermal runaway in commercial energy storage systems.</jats:p>
journal: ACS Nano

title:
Bispecific Nanobody
Broadly Neutralizes and Cross-Protects
against Three Highly Pathogenic Human Coronaviruses
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>SARS-CoV, SARS-CoV-2, and MERS-CoV continue to infect humans or pose a threat of future outbreaks, highlighting the ongoing need for effective, broad-spectrum therapeutics that target these highly pathogenic coronaviruses. As single-domain antibodies, nanobodies have a small size, high target-binding affinity, exceptional stability, low production costs, and the ability to access otherwise hidden or cryptic epitopes. Here, we identified nanobodies targeting SARS-CoV, SARS-CoV-2, and MERS-CoV receptor-binding domains (RBDs) using phage display libraries derived from immunized nanomice and generated a bispecific nanobody to evaluate its broadly neutralizing activity and cross-protective efficacy. Nanobodies 2F11 and 4D6 targeted SARS-CoV RBD, potently neutralizing the SARS-CoV original (Tor2) strain, whereas nanobody 3B11 targeted both SARS-CoV and SARS-CoV-2 RBDs, broadly neutralizing all three SARS-CoV strains (Tor2, GD03, and SZ3) and divergent SARS-CoV-2 variants. Among MERS-CoV RBD-targeting nanobodies, 1C11 demonstrated broadly neutralizing activity against multiple MERS-CoV strains, while its Fc-fused version substantially enhanced the neutralizing potency. These nanobodies exerted neutralizing effects by blocking the interaction between the RBDs and their respective receptors. Cryo-EM structures, computational modeling, and epitope-mapping analyses revealed unique epitopes of 2F11, 3B11, and 1C11 on the SARS-CoV, SARS-CoV-2, or MERS-CoV RBD, underlying their antiviral potency. Finally, a bispecific nanobody 3B11–1C11-Fc that binds to the SARS-CoV, SARS-CoV-2, and MERS-CoV RBDs exhibited high stability and robust cross-neutralizing activity against all tested SARS-CoV, SARS-CoV-2, and MERS-CoV strains, protecting mice from infection with these three coronaviruses. Overall, the identified nanobodies, particularly the bispecific nanobody, exhibit strong neutralizing potency and protective efficacy against SARS-CoV, SARS-CoV-2, and MERS-CoV, showing the potential for further therapeutic development.</jats:p>
journal: ACS Nano

title:
Spacer Cation-Dependent
Interfacial Dynamics in 2D/3D
Perovskites under Electrochemical Bias
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>The integration of two-dimensional (2D) perovskites into three-dimensional (3D) frameworks has been established as an effective strategy to mitigate the intrinsic instability issue of conventional 3D perovskites. However, despite the wide use of spacer cations, less is known about spacer cation-dependent interfacial energetic offsets and their impact on operational stability at a given electrochemical bias. We have now probed charge carrier recombination dynamics at 2D/3D interfaces constructed with two distinct spacer-induced binding motifs: (1) Ruddlesden–Popper phase incorporating butylammonium (BA) and (2) Dion–Jacobson framework formed with 1,4-butanediammonium (BDA) cations. Ultrafast transient absorption spectra recorded under applied electrochemical potentials from −0.2 to +0.4 V versus an Ag/Ag+ reference electrode reveal a different bias-dependent modulation of bleach recovery kinetics at 2D/3D interfaces (BA vs BDA). Interfacial band alignment and potential across interfaces govern the overall charge carrier recombination dynamics. In situ spectroelectrochemical investigations presented in this study provide insight into the critical role of spacer cations in controlling interfacial properties and assist in stabilizing 2D/3D perovskite interfaces.</jats:p>
journal: ACS Nano

title: Iron‐Catalyzed Regioselective Amidation of Pyridines via Zincke Imine Intermediates
content:
An iron‐catalyzed regioselective amidation of Zincke imines enables access to C3‐amidated pyridines, including C2‐, C3‐, C4‐, and disubstituted derivatives. The method features broad functional group tolerance and a telescoped one‐pot protocol from pyridines. Mechanistic and computational studies support a high‐spin Fe(III)–imidyl radical intermediate, revealing a distinct pathway for meta‐selective pyridine amination.








ABSTRACT
Achieving precise site‐selective functionalization of pyridines is highly desirable in synthetic and medicinal chemistry. Herein, we present an operationally simple iron‐catalyzed protocol for accessing C3‐amidated pyridines. The reaction harnesses an in situ‐generated Fe–acylnitrenoid that interacts with Zincke imines, which serve as temporarily dearomatized forms of pyridines. The reaction exhibits broad substrate scope across C2‐, C3‐, C4‐, or disubstituted pyridine substrates. This approach was also successfully implemented in a telescoped one‐pot procedure by directly employing pyridines. Mechanistic and computational studies revealed that a high‐spin Fe(III)–imidyl radical would be the key amidating species.
journal: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents

title: An Oxidative Twist to the Interrupted Pummerer Reaction: Unlocking Inaccessible Aryl Sulfonium Salts
content:
A mechanistically alternative oxidative interrupted Pummerer process was disclosed and the practicality of oxidative variant was demonstrated through the rapid preparation of a diverse array of aryl sulfonium salt, including thianthrenium, dibenzothiophenium, and phenoxathiinium scaffolds.








ABSTRACT
The interrupted Pummerer reaction is a time‐honored and enduringly versatile tool in organic synthesis, and has recently found widespread application in the preparation of aryl sulfonium salts. However, the classical interrupted Pummerer protocol suffers from long‐standing intrinsic limitations: (a) The key reactants, sulfoxides, are rarely commercially available; (b) the use of harsh electrophilic activator often leads to limited functional‐group tolerance. To address these issues, we have herein developed a Selectfluor‐mediated oxidative interrupted Pummerer variant, which is applicable to synthetic C─H functionalization, allowing approaches to a range of aryl sulfonium salts, including thianthrenium, dibenzothiophenium, and phenoxathiinium frameworks. The present strategy circumvents the use of electrophilic activator and directly utilizes sulfides as starting materials, thereby enabling the scope to be expanded to unprotected amine‐containing arenes.
journal: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents

title: Trigonal Prismatic Coordination Field‐Induced d‐Orbital Splitting Enables σ Electron Activation for Efficient Polysulfide Conversion in Li–S Batteries
content:
The NbSe2 was elaborately synthesized to investigate the electron transfer of sublayer transition metal cations. The σ*–σ and π*–σ electron transfer channels at sublayer Nb sites are identified in terms of the coordination field theory and hybrid orbital theory, where the σ*–σ channel exhibits higher electron transfer efficiency, which in turn enhances the role of transition metal sites in polysulfide adsorption and conversion. 








ABSTRACT
Understanding the electron‐transfer pathways and the mechanism in facilitating polysulfide conversion is crucial for the rational design of catalysts in lithium–sulfur batteries. Herein, we designed an NbSe2 model catalyst to investigate the electron‐transfer pathways at sublayer transition metal cation sites through coordination field modulation, and revealed the relationship between electron transfer and catalytic efficiency. Moreover, the σ*–σ and π*–σ electron transfer channels at transition metal sites are identified in terms of the coordination field theory and hybrid orbital theory, where the σ*–σ channel exhibits higher electron transfer efficiency and therefore enhances the adsorption and conversion role of transition metal sites in polysulfides. The designed trigonal prismatic NbSe2 exhibits a reversible capacity up to 799 mAh g−1 at a high rate of 5 C, and the battery maintains stability under ultra‐high sulfur loading, achieving a capacity retention rate as high as 95.85%. From an electronic perspective, this work reveals the role of coordination fields on catalytic activity, providing new insights for the rational design of catalysts in metal–S batteries.
journal: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents

title: Spatial Electrostatic Complementarity in MOF Pores Enables Selective Recognition of Closely Related Fluoromethanes
content:
A spatially organized electrostatic complementary recognition (ECR) environment discriminates the inverted electrostatic patterns of CH3F and CHF3, enabling selective capture of trace CHF3 and high‐purity CH3F production.








ABSTRACT
Trace purification of chemically similar gases is particularly challenging when molecular size and kinetics offer little contrast and conventional affinity descriptors provide conflicting guidance. Trifluoromethane (CHF3) removal from monofluoromethane (CH3F) exemplifies this problem: CH3F has the greater dipole moment, and CHF3 is more polarizable. Here, to our knowledge, we report the first adsorptive removal of trace CHF3 from CH3F and demonstrate electrostatic complementary recognition (ECR) in interpenetrated anion‐pillared MOF pores. Localized, directional negative‐potential sites from TiF62– pillars and surrounding electropositive pyridyl C─H domains complement the 1H/3F electrostatic pattern of CHF3 while geometrically frustrating the inverse 3H/1F pattern of CH3F. All other benchmark adsorbents showed an overall preference for CH3F, whereas both TIFSIX frameworks achieved a reversal of adsorption preference toward CHF3 under trace‐relevant conditions. TIFSIX‐Cu‐dpt, featuring a more focused and directional ECR environment, adsorbed 18.5 cm3/g of CHF3 at 0.1 kPa. Neutron diffraction, adsorption thermodynamics, and molecular simulations support a spatially complementary multipoint binding mode. Fixed‐bed breakthrough of a binary feed containing 1000 ppm CHF3 produced CH3F with >99.999% purity relative to CHF3 at 320 L/kg. These results show how spatial electrostatic complementarity can translate subtle molecular differences beyond conventional scalar descriptors into selective adsorption.
journal: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents

title: Photocatalytic Disruption of Concurrent Redox Axes Elicits Convergent Redox Collapse
content:
A biosafe organic photocatalyst disrupts interconnected redox axes via photocatalysis of NADPH and GSH, eliciting convergent redox collapse in cancer cells.








ABSTRACT
The interconnected antioxidant systems of cancer cells, centered on the glutathione and thioredoxin axes, constitute a promising therapeutic vulnerability. However, simultaneous disruption of both axes by dual‐inhibitor regimens is hampered by pharmacokinetic asynchrony. Herein, we report squaraine‐based photocatalysts as a single‐agent modality that concurrently disrupts these interconnected antioxidant systems in cancer cells. Upon 635 nm light irradiation, IITC depletes intracellular NADPH and GSH through photocatalytic oxidation coupled with type I/II photosensitization. NADPH depletion deprives the reductive coenzyme of thioredoxin reductase in the thioredoxin axis, while glutathione oxidation collapses the central antioxidant axis. Consequently, IITC ablates both antioxidant axes concurrently and exerts potent phototherapeutic anticancer activity in vitro and in vivo. Importantly, during phototherapy IITC undergoes self‐immolation into nontoxic degraded fragments, thereby avoiding phototoxicity post‐treatment. This self‐eliminating, metabolism‐targeted photocatalytic strategy establishes a new avenue for safe and efficient cancer phototherapy.
journal: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents

title: Robust Tetrazine‐Bridged Binuclear Iridium(III) Complex Featuring Tunable Conformational Dynamics for Efficient Photothermal Conversion
content:
Shaking the Energy Out: A stable binuclear iridium(III) complex with a bridging s‐tetrazine ligand shows ultra‐broad near‐infrared absorption up to 1200 nm in solution and 1500 nm in solid. Crystal packing engineering enables unlocking “butterfly‐like” intramolecular motion. This activates non‐radiative relaxation pathways, delivering an excellent photothermal conversion efficiency of up to 95%.








ABSTRACT
Developing near‐infrared photothermal materials with outstanding conversion efficiency and high photostability remains a critical challenge for small‐molecule systems. We report a unique donor‐acceptor platform based on a binuclear iridium(III) architecture featuring a bridging electron‐deficient 1,2,4,5‐tetrazine ligand. The complex exhibits strong and broad absorption up to 1200 nm in solution and 1500 nm in the solid state, significantly outperforming other metal complexes. Temperature‐ and solvent‐dependent 1H NMR coupled with X‐ray diffraction suggest the ‘butterfly‐like’ conformational behavior of the complex, while theoretical calculations identify low‐energy charge‐transfer transitions from cyclometalated cores to the tetrazine moiety as the origin of the exceptionally high absorbance and efficient non‐radiative relaxation. This facilitates robust photothermal activity across three different excitation wavelengths (635, 808, 980 nm), delivering an excellent conversion efficiency of 94.9% at 808 nm (acetone solvate) along with long‐term stability over multiple cycles (CHCl3/CH2Cl2‐derived phase), uniquely tunable through crystal packing engineering. When applied to cellulose paper, the complex drives solar‐to‐thermal water evaporation with an efficiency of 86.6%. This high performance is accompanied by exceptional photostability under prolonged irradiation, ranking the developed material among the most competitive systems reported. Overall, this work establishes bridging 1,2,4,5‐tetrazines and crystal engineering as powerful tools for designing high‐performance organometallic photothermal materials.
journal: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents

title: A Phosphonium Relay for Integrated Cleavage‐to‐Cyclization of Cyclic Peptides
content:
A phosphonium‐mediated relay directly couples cleavage from standard 2‐CTC resin with C‐terminal activation and head‐to‐tail peptide macrocyclization. The linker‐free workflow avoids isolation of linear intermediates and high‐dilution conditions, tolerates diverse peptide substrates and functional handles, and integrates readily with automated synthesis, providing an efficient route to cyclic peptides, including hydrophobic and poorly soluble targets.








ABSTRACT
Head‐to‐tail macrocyclization of peptides is typically performed through stepwise workflows that separate resin cleavage, isolation of linear intermediates, and subsequent cyclization, largely due to incompatible activation requirements for each transformation. Here we report a phosphonium‐mediated relay that unifies these steps within a single activation node. In this design, an electrophile‐activated phosphonium species promotes cleavage from standard 2‐chlorotrityl chloride (2‐CTC) resin and is proposed to enable in situ formation of a C‐terminally activated intermediate for intramolecular amidation. The strategy directly couples cleavage to cyclization on standard peptide supports without auxiliary linkers, intermediate purification, or high‐dilution cyclization conditions. The method is compatible with diverse peptide sequccnces and functional handles and can be integrated into a closed‐loop automated workflow for end‐to‐end synthesis, with advantages for hydrophobic substrates by avoiding isolation of poorly soluble linear intermediates such as Vespid chemotactic peptide 5f. Process‐level benchmarking against side‐chain anchoring further demonstrated favorable process metrics and gram‐scale scalability. This work establishes a linker‐free cleavage‐to‐cyclization strategy and provides a practical framework for integrated and automation‐compatible cyclic peptide synthesis.
journal: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents

title: Photo‐Induced Multi‐Physical Field Synergy for Direct Natural Seawater Electrolysis
content:
Photo‐induced multi‐physical fields dynamically regulate interfacial OH− transfer, eliminating cathode pH self‐amplifying polarization. The photo‐responsive catalytic platform was engineered to integrate asymmetric electric fields and disrupt the hydrogen‐bond network. Alloy localized heating induces micro‐scale thermal convection. These strategies synergistically suppress precipitation and enhance catalytic performance, thus realizing efficient natural seawater splitting.








ABSTRACT
Direct natural seawater electrolysis offers a sustainable route for green hydrogen production, yet severe performance degradation stemming from irreversible interfacial precipitation hinders its practical application. Herein, a photo‐induced multi‐physical field synergy strategy is developed to dynamically regulate interfacial OH− transfer and eliminate cathode pH self‐amplifying polarization. A plasmonic photo‐responsive electrode constructed via ultrathin amorphous MoO3 coating on PtMo alloy nanoparticles is fabricated to integrate photo‐induced asymmetric electric field (PAEF) and localized photothermal field (PLPF). Such a well‐designed core‐shell structure delivers a record‐high industrial current density of 8 A cm−2 at low overpotential (433 mV) in alkaline seawater. In situ characterizations and spectroscopic analyses verify that the dual fields optimize the electric double‐layer ion distribution and drive microscale thermal convection, accelerating OH− dissipation. Benefiting from the above, the engineered light‐responsive catalytic system exhibits a low overpotential of 232 mV at 100 mA cm−2 in natural seawater, alongside anti‐precipitation ability, and maintains stable operation over 100 h (6.2% decay). A photo‐assisted asymmetric electrolyzer achieves a low cell voltage of 2.27 V at 0.5 A cm−2 for seawater splitting, which realizes effective green hydrogen generation under fluctuating natural solar light (normalized ramp‐following ratio > 0.9).
journal: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents

title: One Carbon Matters: Conformational Bending Stabilizes Ferroelectric Nematic Order and Enables Domain‐Modulated Antiferroelectric Smectic C Order
content:
A single‐carbon modification reshapes the conformational landscape of polar mesogens, transforming rod‐like molecules into more bent, pear‐like architectures that stabilize ferroelectric nematic order. Further extension of the flexible segment induces bent packing and domain‐modulated antiferroelectric smectic C organization.








ABSTRACT
Molecular design of ferroelectric nematics has primarily focused on optimizing highly polar rigid mesogenic cores, whereas the role of flexible aliphatic segments in regulating molecular conformation and polar ordering remains insufficiently understood. Here, we show that exchanging the positions of a methylene group and the ether oxygen within the linkage between a polar rigid core and an aliphatic tail (Ar‐O‐CH2‐ versus Ar‐CH2‐O‐) reshapes the molecular conformational landscape and profoundly influences the stability of the ferroelectric nematic (NF) phase. Molecules with a stronger preference for bent, pear‐like effective geometries exhibit significantly enhanced NF stability, accompanied by reduced splay and bend elastic constants in the apolar nematic phase, and lower apparent activation barriers for dipolar reorientation. Further elongation of the flexible segment introduces competing packing motifs and gives rise to a domain‐modulated antiferroelectric smectic C (SmCAF) phase. These findings establish conformational bending as a molecular‐shape parameter for controlling hierarchical ferroelectric and antiferroelectric liquid‐crystalline order, bridging the design principles of conventional bent‐core layered ferroelectrics with emerging rod‐like fluid ferroelectric materials.
journal: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents

title: Revisiting the Role of Dynamic Linkages in Polymer Compatibilization Using Diazirine–Anhydride Conjugates
content:
Reactive molecular dynamics simulations, together with experiments performed using matched pairs of anhydride–diazirine conjugates, reveal no persistent advantage for dynamic linkages in reactive compatibilization of blended polymers. On the contrary, the existence of dynamic exchange can lead to disproportionation of hetero‐crosslinked structures—which support compatibilization—into homo‐crosslinked aggregates—which disfavor compatibilization.








ABSTRACT
Small‐molecule crosslinkers can compatibilize mixed plastics through reactive extrusion, providing a potential solution to extant challenges in polymer recycling. Existing studies have prioritized the use of crosslinker molecules that incorporate dynamic linkages between reactive warheads; however, the absolute requirement for these dynamic groups remains unproven, and previous comparisons of static versus dynamic crosslinkers employed molecules with vastly different C–H insertion efficiencies. In this study, we employed chemistry‐explicit reaction molecular dynamics simulations, small‐molecule surrogates of interface reactions, phase morphology studies, and mechanical analysis to explicitly test hypotheses around the value of dynamic linkages. Using rationally designed, reactivity‐matched pairs of dynamic and static crosslinkers, we found the presence of dynamic anhydride linkages did not generally improve compatibilization efficacy. Instead, dynamic exchange enabled reorganization of compatibilizing hetero‐crosslinks into non‐compatibilizing homo‐crosslinks over time, while facilitating other undesirable reactivity pathways. Our findings indicate compatibilization performance is dictated by physicochemical control over crosslinker distribution, rather than dynamic bonding, and that the kinetics of dynamic exchange must be tightly regulated to avoid undermining compatibilization. We anticipate that these findings will guide the development of improved crosslinker reagents for polymer compatibilization and other materials applications.

title: Anionic Lone‐Pair‐Like Electrons Induced Ultra‐Low Lattice Thermal Conductivity and High Thermoelectric Performance
content:
Unlike cationic lone pairs, which are confined to specific cations (e.g., Sb3+) and reduce lattice thermal conductivity by enhancing anharmonicity, our work demonstrates that this lone‑pair strategy can be extended to anions in CuInSnSe4. This leads to an extremely low lattice thermal conductivity of 0.55 W m−1 K−1 at 773 K through a distinct mechanism involving localized optical phonon modes.








ABSTRACT
The traditional lone‐pair electron strategy primarily reduces lattice thermal conductivity (κL) by enhancing anharmonic lattice vibrations. However, this mechanism has long been considered to exist only in specific cations with ns2 electron configurations (e.g. Sb3+, Bi3+), severely restricting the broader applicability of this lone‐pair‐based approach. In this study, CuInSnSe4 is successfully synthesized via atomic cross‐substitution from the diamondoid CuInSe2, wherein the Se atoms exhibit an anionic lone‐pair‐like electronic behavior, revealing a new approach to reducing κL that differs from conventional cation‐based mechanisms. In contrast to the traditional mechanism that relies on cations to enhance lattice anharmonicity, the anionic lone‐pair electrons weaken the Se‐Se interactions, flatten the optical phonon branches, and consequently significantly expand the scattering phase space, providing more scattering channels for phonons. This anionic lone‐pair electron strategy reduces the room‐temperature κL from 4.48 to 1.26 W m−1 K−1. Ultimately, the predicted optimal thermoelectric figure of merit (ZT) for p‐type and n‐type CuInSnSe4 attains values of 1.99 and 0.79, respectively. This work systematically expands the conventional application boundaries of the lone‐pair electron strategy and elucidates a fundamentally distinct mechanism for κL reduction, providing a new theoretical basis for designing and developing novel high‐efficiency thermoelectric materials with intrinsically low κL.
journal: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents

title: An In Situ Amorphous Thermoconversion Strategy for Macroscopic Glass Heterojunctions
content:
A new family of macroscopic hybrid glass heterojunctions has been constructed in situ through an amorphous thermoconversion strategy. By exploiting the structural competition among liquid phases derived from distinct metal–organic hybrid halide crystals, these glasses exhibit persistent luminescence with color tunability, thus offering multi‐channel optical waveguide and programmable emission‐color sequences for information encryption.








ABSTRACT
Heterojunction fabrication has long been constrained by the stringent lattice‐matching requirements between dissimilar components, limiting the accessible material combinations and processing routes. Here, we report an amorphous thermoconversion strategy for constructing hybrid glass heterojunctions in situ. In this approach, structural competition among liquid phases derived from distinct metal–organic hybrid halide crystal structures generates divergent luminescence across amorphous phases, giving rise to a new family of halide glass heterojunctions. These hybrid halide glasses display excitation‐dependent and time‐gated persistent luminescence that is color‐tunable across a 160 nm wavelength window, a property that enables direct optical visualization and confers broad photonic versatility. Beyond their optical attributes, the resulting macroscopic glass heterojunctions exhibit well‐defined mechanical rigidity and arbitrary processability, supporting spatially resolved fluorescence and persistent luminescence outputs alongside one‐dimensional (1D) optical waveguiding at losses that surpass those of state‐of‐the‐art crystalline counterparts. Therefore, this work delivers the demonstration of macroscopic heterojunctions in halide supramolecular glasses and establishes a scalable route to multi‐channel, low‐dimensional optical waveguide for information storage and encryption applications.
journal: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents

title: In Situ Spectroscopic Monitoring of Laser Sintered Gold Nanoparticle Microelectrodes
content:
The combined use of a laser source as a spectroscopic and patterning tool enables the in situ monitoring of conductive network formation, as gold nanoparticles coalesce during microelectrode fabrication. The platform can be extended to non‐flat and microscale substrates, as demonstrated through the integration of bioinspired multifunctional sensors onto hair‐sized microtubes.








ABSTRACT
Laser sources are commonly used for resist‐free electrode patterning via metal nanoparticle sintering and for spectroscopic analysis. The intersection between these applications, however, is relatively unexplored. Here, in situ Raman spectroscopy is performed to elucidate the state of gold nanoparticles during the laser sintering of conductive micrometer‐ and sub‐micrometer‐scale electrodes. First, we establish the conditions under which sample integrity is preserved during Raman spectroscopy. As the laser intensity is increased, the Raman band intensity associated with organic ligands surrounding the gold nanoparticles first increases and then decreases, providing an in situ probe of sintering progress. The rise and fall in Raman band intensity is associated with surface‐enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) caused by changes in nanoparticle size and spacing as sintering progresses. Conductive atomic force microscopy and scanning electron microscopy (SEM) reveal the evolution of the electrically connected gold nanoparticle networks as a function of laser sintering intensity. By tuning the laser focus, we demonstrate bioinspired, multifunctional chemical and strain sensor fabrication on flexible microtubes with the diameter of a human hair. These advances highlight the potential of combined Raman laser spectroscopy and patterning for sintering process development and device integration on unconventional substrates.

title: Cell Membrane‐Coated Nanoplatforms for Radiosensitizer Delivery in Precision Cancer Radiotherapy
content:
This review summarizes the biological basis of radiosensitization and major radiosensitizer classes, then highlights biomimetic delivery platforms for improved tumor targeting, microenvironment modulation, and immune activation. Cell membrane‐coated nanoplatforms integrate precise radiosensitizer delivery with microenvironment regulation to enhance radiotherapy, with future efforts needed in membrane engineering, multifunctional design, and clinical translation.








ABSTRACT
Tumor radiotherapy is one of the core modalities in comprehensive clinical cancer treatment. However, the inherent radiation resistance of tumor cells, radiotherapy resistance mediated by the tumor microenvironment, and irreversible damage to normal tissues caused by radiotherapy severely limit its clinical efficacy. Although various radiosensitizers have been developed to enhance radiation‐induced tumor damage, their clinical translation largely depends on efficient and tumor‐specific delivery systems. This review first summarizes the biological basis of radiosensitization and the major classes of radiosensitizers and then focuses on recent advances in biomimetic delivery platforms designed to improve tumor targeting, microenvironment modulation, and immune activation. Collectively, cell membrane‐coated biomimetic nanoplatforms represent a promising strategy for integrating precise radiosensitizer delivery with tumor microenvironment modulation to enhance radiotherapy efficacy. Future work should be dedicated to optimizing membrane engineering, designing multifunctional nanoparticles, and developing manufacturing strategies for clinical translation, thereby accelerating their implementation in precision radiotherapy.
